utterances.text: It says unequivocally here that the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina defends the sovereignty territorial integrity, independence, and constitutional order of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina because that is what it was called in the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have to read it because, as I said, it is written here and the Judges are aware of it. The parties are also aware of what is written here. Now I'm going to ask you about Article 2. You don't have to read it out loud. You, as a former JNA officer, what did you do in the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I was a professional soldier in the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Article 3, the term "active-duty personnel" is used. Did you consider yourself an active-duty person in the Army of Republika Srpska on the basis of this law?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: In the Yugoslav People's Army, I think that we were called active military officers while we were in the JNA. Later on, the term "professional" was introduced so then that created a bit of confusion. We don't know exactly in which period what term was used, but it's basically one in the same thing, active-duty officer and professional officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just asked you whether you consider yourself to be an active-duty military officer on the basis of this article of the army -- the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Active-duty military personnel, yes, we simply copied that term that was well established by then. It's not that we invented it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Article 4 speaks of relations within the service, and I already asked you who your superior was and you told us. Did you have a subordinate in the Army of Republika Srpska according to this law? Did you have anyone who was subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: In the Army of Republika Srpska, there was the principle of subordination and singleness of command. As chief of the personnel department, I had my superior and I had my subordinates, and these were persons who worked in the personnel department where I was chief or head.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have a look at Article 153. In B/C/S it's page 15 and in English it's 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Article 153 speaks of assignment of duties, and it says: Active military personnel should be assigned to military units and institutions and should be appointed to appropriate duties, i.e., establishment posts, according to the needs of the service? Who is it that appoints a military person on the basis of this law?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: According to this law, it is the officer in charge on the basis of a decision of the minister of defence is the one who appoints active-duty military personnel in accordance with the person's rank and education.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In which army?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: In the Army of Republika Srpska. Here it says in the Army of Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but that's one in the same army, just different names were used in different periods.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us just look at Article 156. We are going to need it later on in relation to some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's on the next page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This article speaks about the notion of stand-in officer. Can you tell us what this means and how this was regulated in the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: An officer who is temporarily prevented from exercising his duties, most often due to health reasons, can be replaced, so to speak, by a stand-in officer who will perform his duties until his return to duty. The second paragraph says that a stand-in may be appointed to a vacant establishment post as well and that this could last for six months based on the decision of the immediate superior and then for another six months if this post is not filled. So the stand-in can only remain in this post for up to a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were these the regulations that an officer in charge in the VRS regulated state related issues for active-duty personnel?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: The Law of the Army of the VRS served as the basis in terms of regulations that governed the appointment in the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now look at Article 369. B/C/S page 36, English page 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Article 369, which deals with competence for addressing relations in the service. You don't need to read it out. I'm mostly interested in promotions. Under this law, who was deciding on the promotions to the rank of general, and who decided on promotions to lower ranks?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Decrees on appointment to the rank of generals was issued by the president of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: That was President Radovan Karadzic. The rank of the colonel and their status-related issues were decided by the minister of defence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as stipulated in this law. Promotions to other ranks from sergeant to lieutenant-colonel was decided by the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS. I'm going to use the term VRS because the previous one lasted only for a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have finished with this document for now. We are now going to move to another topic. Mr. Malcic, can you tell us, how did you receive your salary while you were in the JNA in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: As an active-duty officer of the JNA serving in the Sarajevo garrison centre for higher education, I received my salary through the military computer centre of the JNA. At the time, we had several such centres in Belgrade, Zagreb, Sarajevo, and I think there was one in Ljubljana and Macedonia. I can't remember now whether I received it directly in Sarajevo or whether it went through Belgrade because I was directly subordinate to the chief for the ground army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the period before the war broke out in 1991 and 1992, how did you receive your salary in practical terms? Did you receive it in cash or was it transferred to your account? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: For quite a while before the war, active-duty officers and civilians serving in the army received their salaries exclusively through current accounts that they had in the Post Savings Bank that had branches in other towns as well. We had one such branch in Sarajevo. We had cheques, we had a chequebook, and we could cash them in any post office everywhere in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you became a member of the Army of Republika Srpska, did you continue to receive your salary in the same manner?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: When I became a member of the VRS, my current account was used to transfer all my salaries and all the fringe benefits that I was entitled to. And I had this account, as I said, in the Post Savings Bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At one point in time, were there any problems with the clearance and payment system? Did you have any problem with cashing in your cheques in the Post Savings Bank?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I know that there was a period of time when the system of payments was disrupted, and I think that was immediately after the war began. We could, during this period of time, cash in our cheques in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. All the families who fled to the FRY, or, rather, some members of the families had authorisation as a kind of secondary current account card and were able to withdraw money.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your family was in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How did you solve this problem?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: We who had families living in Republika Srpska were not able to withdraw our salaries from the post offices in Republika Srpska due to the severance of the system of payment. Then we, the active personnel and the civilians serving in the Army of Republika Srpska, gave a proxy to the financial organ of the Army of Republika Srpska to enable them to go directly to the Post Savings Bank and withdraw cash from our current accounts and bring it to us at our command in the Army of Republika Srpska and distribute the money. The currency at the time was dinar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is what you did concerning your family who was living in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, whenever an officer would go from Han Pijesak to Banja Luka, I would take this opportunity to give him some money to take it to my family. Later on, I thought and I realised that it was much simpler to authorise this officer who was collecting salaries for the Banja Luka garrison to withdraw this money and take it directly to my family in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time, was it important to get this cash in hand as soon as possible after it has been paid into your account?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, from the summer of 1992 onwards until almost the end of 1993, there was hyperinflation in Republika Srpska. Money was devalued overnight. Therefore, it was very important for the end user to get the cash as soon as possible in order to be able to buy staple food and other necessities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who among members of the VRS was receiving their salary in this fashion?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: You mean in this way that I just described? All the active-duty personnel and the civilians serving in the Army of Republika Srpska did that. As far as I know, this system of payment was the same for members of the VJ. They continued to receive their salaries through the Post Savings Bank. Nothing changed in the system compared to the previous period.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say active-duty personnel or active-duty officers, what other kind of officers and non-commissioned officers existed in the VRS? Was there any other category?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: In addition to active-duty personnel consisting of officers and non-commissioned officers who had finished various military schools, among members of the VRS we had reserve officers and non-commissioned officers. But during the war we didn't use the terms "active" or "non-active." It was important for them to have proper education and to perform their duties and tasks in a proper manner. For the most part, there were -- those were trained officers who finished the school of reserve officers in the JNA before the war or had college or university degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who paid their salaries?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: These officers and non-commissioned officers, just like soldiers of the VRS, received salaries from the ministry of defence of the VRS under the rules of salaries and other entitlements of Republika Srpska. Initially, these were just symbolic amounts because part of the salary was paid out in kind. They received fuel, oil, garments, and other items that were distributed in the places where their families lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What happened with members of the former JNA who had retired and who remained in the -- in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: A number of retired members of the JNA who remained in Bosnia-Herzegovina later moved to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Those were, for the most part, officers who lived in the territories held by the TO and the HVO. The officers who remained living in Republika Srpska, the retired officers, I mean, were also receiving their pensions through the Post Savings Bank. Those who fled to the FRY could cash in their cheques in all branches of the Post Savings Banks. And those who lived in Republika Srpska, I'm not sure, but I think that they made similar arrangements as we did for our families. They sent one person who collected the money for all of them and then distributed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you still have social security and health insurance when you became a member of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: As a member of the VRS, I received my salary to the Post Savings Bank in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. On that basis, certain amounts were earmarked for health insurance and social security, and we were entitled to health care and social security in the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did your family members use the same benefits in terms of health insurance?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the places where they found accommodation. There was a problem with that, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now have a break, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Malcic, before the break I asked you whether family members enjoyed the same benefits in relation to health insurance. You said that there was some problem in that regard. Could you please tell us what the problem was in relation to health insurance and the entitlements of families?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: On the basis of my own health insurance, my family members were also entitled to health insurance. My wife and my two daughters, or, actually, my wife had health insurance through the company that she worked in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In order to be entitled to health insurance, does an insuree have a document? And if, so what is the document called?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to say, there was no problem for me because I had my health booklet, as it was known, and I had it certified at the Main Staff and I gave it to the members of my family who were in Banja Luka and they could be treated at the military medical facilities in Banja Luka. However, there was a problem for the members of families who fled to the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. They didn't know where they could have their health booklets stamped or where they could get new ones, if they forgot their original ones when leaving the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Also, they didn't know in which institutions they could be treated. They tried to make due in different ways. I don't know, it depended on the individual involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to the rules of the former JNA, where were health booklets stamped and thus certified?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Health booklets of active-duty personnel and their family members were stamped at the personnel organ of their unit. It was the personnel organ that was in charge of dealing with status related matters for such an individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know, Mr. Malcic, what happened to the units of the former JNA that were located in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina and then went to the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia? Basically, did the 2nd Military District continue to exist after the army was established and these units that were part of it?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: According to the order, or, rather, decision of the Presidency of the SFRY in April 1992, all units of the JNA were duty-bound to withdraw to the territory of the FRY, and it was the organ in charge that decided which garrison every unit should go to. They were put up there temporarily as far as I know, because at that time the establishment of the Army of Yugoslavia was being developed as well. Just like other units, they fitted into the units of the Army of Yugoslavia. That is what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We already heard some testimony here, but perhaps you could tell us which elements comprised the salary of an officer in the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: An active-duty military person in the former JNA had a salary that consisted of the following parts: It depended on rank, position group, and benefits, such as army benefit that all military personnel were entitled to, troops benefit only for officers who served in troops; and then also other benefits like the air force and the navy, they had special benefits within their salaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any other benefits that officers of the JNA enjoyed as well as the services?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: They had the right to compensation for separation if they lived separate from their families and if they could not provide accommodation for their families once they were transferred to a new garrison. Also they had benefits if they served in areas where it was exceptionally difficult to serve like hardship posts and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That will do, thank you. Did they have the right to accommodation? How was that regulated?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: According to regulations of the JNA, they had the right to housing, that is to say, they would be allotted apartments from the housing fund, the military housing fund. From our gross salaries, certain amounts were earmarked for that, like for pension insurance, health insurance, and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Malcic, you lived in an apartment in Sarajevo and you told us that after that your family moved to Banja Luka. Were you the owner of that apartment in Sarajevo, the one that you left behind?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I got the apartment from the military housing fund of the Sarajevo garrison of the JNA, and it was precisely in the beginning of 1992 that certain procedures started allowing persons to purchase apartments according to a law that was passed at that time. Up until the beginning of the war, I had purchased my apartment. I had made all the payments necessary. However, I didn't manage to have it registered in the records of immovable property of the City of Sarajevo because at that time these records or log-books had not been established yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Not to go into too great details, did you sell the apartment later and was it sold at its market price when it was ultimately sold?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I'm one of the few military officers who managed to get his apartment back in Sarajevo. It was sometime in 2004, I'm not quite sure. Thanks to a good lawyer who helped me at the time. Many of my colleagues to this day have not managed to have their apartments given to them by the Sarajevo garrison returned to them, and I believe that they will never succeed in doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you sell it at the market price at the time, at least approximately?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I sold it at the time below its market value just to get any kind of money for it so that I could use that money to build my own house in Banja Luka and thus have a home for myself and my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I'd like to move on to some other documents and certain procedures involved in the work you did before personnel centres were established. And then we are going to see what it was that you did once they were established. First I'm going to ask you whether you know approximately when the 30th Personnel Centre of the Army of Yugoslavia was established, roughly?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, towards the end of 1993, the 30th Personnel Centre was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said that you received your salary in the way in which you described once you joined the Army of Republika Srpska. During that period before the personnel centres were established, let's just say until the end of 1993, was your salary somehow made to match your change in status in the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: At first I only received my salary on the basis of the elements of the job I had in the JNA before the war. It was only towards the end of 1992 once appointments were made in the Army of Republika Srpska. We started receiving salary on the basis of position group as well. We submitted that to the information technology centre and we told them what our duties were. However, we could only submit the appointment orders where the position group could be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, sir, the interpreter is struggling to keep pace with you. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They did not recognise our ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say the information technology centre or computer centre, where is it? In Yugoslavia or in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: In Yugoslavia. That was the centre that had calculated our salaries earlier on as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 57, line 25, perhaps we should use the term that was used before, the "accounting centre," I think the witness used the word "military accounting centre." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was it that you sent? Which document did you send to that military accounting or computer centre? I'm asking you about the period --

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: In our work we used all forms and regulations of the JNA that we found in the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. They were gathered there in different ways. Some things came from Sarajevo, other things came from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I wasn't clear. What document is it in terms of form?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought it was regulations that you were asking me about. The document was the appointment order on the basis of which we compile a report on the hand-over of duty. We would send that to the computer centre or accounting centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like us to have a look at two documents. The first document is from our 65 ter list. The Defence [In English] 00191D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a decree of the president of the republic -- the president of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic Radovan Karadzic dated the 31st of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just scroll down to see who signed the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Malcic, on the basis of which regulations --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have it scrolled up a bit now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the basis of which regulations of which state was this document passed?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Decree of the president of the Presidency of the Serb Republic, as it says here, of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was passed on the basis of the Law on the Army of Republika Srpska. It was signed by the president of Republika Srpska Radovan Karadzic, and the officer involved was Svetislav Galic, and he was commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. This was a unit within the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did this document arrive at your personnel office at one point in time?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: A certified copy arrived in my office and then on the basis of this decree a report was written up on the hand-over of duty for General Galic. And then he would take that to his superior officer to confirm it, and that was General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a number assigned to this document, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, I heard the witness saying at page 59, line 4: "Decree of the president of the Presidency of the Serb republic, as it says here, of Bosnia-Herzegovina." Where does it say "of Bosnia-Herzegovina"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's written here in an abbreviated form, but it just says Srpska Republika. But it was Srpska Republika BH; that is what it was known as at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00294, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is a dated the 31st of August, 1992. Can we now look at the next document which is number 65 ter 00190D. This is a document issued by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps on the 31st of August, 1992. The title is "Report on the Hand-Over of Duty." It was signed by General Ratko Mladic and Colonel Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please comment on this document. Is that the document that you mentioned earlier that accompanies the other one?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Upon receipt of the decree on appointment, the personnel organ of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps made this document based on the decree. It precisely states the date on which General Galic took over the duty of the commander of the corps. It says here, On the 31st of August, 1992, I took over the duty of commander of Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. It contains all the elements necessary to calculate the salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please slow down. This is very important. Now, tell us something about these elements. Where is it stipulated here?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please zoom out the B/C/S version so that the witness can see the whole document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Malcic, they request that you don't touch the screen with your finger. You can point, but don't touch the screen because when you do touch the screen it causes problems for them. I also don't understand. Okay. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document, can you point to the information that affects the salary?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: First of all, establishment rank, it says here major-general, Position Group 6. These are very important elements for calculating one's salary. Underneath it says that in this establishment book of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, according to establishment, the establishment rank of lieutenant-colonel falls into the category of Position Group 5. That means that Galic did not receive the salary consistent with the elements of a commander of a corps because previously he had Position Group 8 and with this appointment he could only have received Group 6, whereas he would be assigned to Group 5 only after he has spent a certain period of time in that position and depending on the performance appraisal. That means that he was going to exercise this right only at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that this document was signed by his superior?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: His superior officer, according to the chain of command. The decree signed by the officer in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, what happens next with this document. Where is it sent?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: The Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command sends this document to my personnel department, and through our financial organ one copy is sent to the computer centre -- or military accounting and computer centre of the VJ. It also changed its name, so I don't know exactly how it was called at this particular time. But the customary return was military computer centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I see you looking at us. I thought maybe I could get the answer without having to ask the parties. These salary ranks, 5 and 6, which one is higher, which one gives you more money, the lower you go or the upper you go with the figures? I'm asking because the witness said was originally rank 8 now he was not paid according to rank 8, and now he is rank 5 then he will get the better money later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me, it was difficult for me too to fathom all these numbers and figures. I don't even know if I understand it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lower rank carries higher salary.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The higher the rank, the lower the salary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The higher the rank, the lower the salary. Or the higher the rank in numbers here?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The higher the rank group, the lower the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So if I'm 8, I'm a junior officer to number 6?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. If I'm one of the top guys --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The person who has Group 1 has the best salary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it would be beneficiary for the Chamber to repeat this answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Malcic, I asked you what happens next with this document. Where is it distributed?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: The document is then sent to the military computer centre for calculating the salaries according to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where was this computer centre, in which state?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: It was in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know according to which rules and regulations the people in Belgrade checked whether this was in order? What were the relevant information for them?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: They abided by the regulations applicable to the Yugoslav Army. We could only receive salaries if our appointments were in compliance with the VJ regulations because our book of rules was so to say such that could -- afforded us better salaries; however, we had to apply these rules and regulations as was the case with the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us take an example. You said that Colonel Galic, who previously had Group 8, could not reach more than Group 5. He could only go up two groups in the hierarchy that affect the salary?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: That was the consequence of the rules applicable to the VJ. According to our rules, he could have got the same group immediately, and I'm talking about the regulations of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If it were to happen that your personnel department --

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: You mean the personnel department of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. If you would notice that something was inconsistent with the VJ regulations, what would you do?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: We would send it back to be corrected so that the person in question can exercise his rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This stamp that you see on the left-hand side which says certified to be in order, who did that?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I think that this was done by the computer centre controller confirming that everything was done in accordance with the law and that this person can be given this group. If he found something to be wrong, he would have returned the document to me and then we would have to correct it, otherwise, it would not be acted upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have an exhibit number for this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D00295, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at document from Defence 65 ter list 00157D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is a document issued by the minister of defence of Republika Srpska on 8th October, 1993, appointing Vinko Pandurevic, commander of the 1st Zvornik Motorised Brigade. Mr. Malcic, this document, if we compare it to the previous ones, is it the same if it is issued by the minister of defence? Does it bear the same consequences with regard to your activities and the salary calculations?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Complete identical, only we have a different officer here, and it's Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on this document, can you say on which date he was appointed to this post?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: The order is dated the 8th of October, 1993, appointing him commander of the Zvornik Brigade. We cannot see the exact date on which he took over the duty. We have to go for that purpose to a different document on hand-over of the duty which confirms by him and his superior that he took over the duty on a specific date.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this a document of Republika Srpska or Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can with we please have an exhibit number for this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D00296, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like now please document from Defence 65 ter list, 00158D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a bit blurred, but this is a report on hand-over of duty by Vinko Pandurevic, dated 25th of October, 1993. Was this document dispatched through you or maybe somebody else to the FRY computer centre?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Through regular channels, it should receive my department after which I would give it to the finance organ for implementation. Initially, there were instances in order to curtail the procedure that the finance organ of the Drina Corps directly sent it to the computer centre or to the General Staff, provided they were absolutely sure that the document was correct. But they did provide me with a copy for information only.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you record such documents in your department?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did, about every take-over of duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are now going to move to the period when the personnel centres were formed. But before that, prior to the establishment of the personnel centre, did you and your fellow officers have problems with the records of members of the VRS who were dispatched to you? Did you have any problems at all with these records?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: In 1992 and for a part of 1993, we were unable to collect complete information for every officer who served in the VRS because it was impossible to obtain DPP 2. All the information that we accumulated were generated on the basis of questionnaires filled in by officers serving in the VRS and some other auxiliary documents that we managed to get our hands on, therefore mistakes happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anyone ever leave units of the VRS without permission, without you knowing that?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were such instances.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Malcic, the interpreter asks that you repeat the answer. They didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were cases of officers leaving their units without permission, that is to say, leaving the Army of Republika Srpska. We didn't know where such officers went because there was no order through which we could check whether they went and joined the Yugoslav Army. That caused great difficulties for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A few moments ago in response to my question you said that towards the end of 1993 you heard that personnel centres were established, specifically we will be dealing with the 30th Personnel Centre. Do you remember now who you heard this from, that the 30th Personnel Centre had been established? What kind of information did you receive?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: It was communicated to me orally by Mico Grubor, my superior officer. He told me that the 30th Personnel Centre was established and that from then on we would have a particular person from whom we would be able to receive accurate information about every active-duty military person serving in the Army of Republika Srpska. Instructions would follow as to how we would be doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear then or later where this 30th Personnel Centre was, who it was subordinated to, which organ?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I heard then that the 30th Personnel Centre would be within the personnel administration of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just not forget, I believe, Your Honours, that I did not tender the previous document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have not tendered this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this one that we have on the screen now. Yes, I would like to tender that. That's what I actually meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00297, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the actual offices of the 30th Personnel Centre were?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I do know. These were two offices that were in one of the buildings within the compound of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you go there personally?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who you contacted there? Do you know who the person in charge was, the person that you contacted?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I contacted Colonel Gojko Mijic who was head of that organ there. There were four or five other people there as well, military officers and civilians. All of these active-duty officers were born in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. For the most part, they were disabled persons or persons who could not do full military service due to their health conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which army did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: They belonged to the Army of Republika Srpska. They just worked there. They did that work in order to meet our needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the name you said -- yes, right.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Gojko Mijic from the area around Banja Luka and Jovo Milicic from the area around Sipovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who their superior officer was?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Truth to tell, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of a man by the name of Dusan Zoric?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I know that General Dusan Zoric was head of the personnel administration of the the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you don't know whether he was their superior?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: I don't really want to engage in guess-work. I wasn't really interested if that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Gojko Mijic or any of his colleagues from there, did they come to see you in Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Most often it was Gojko Mijic who came in relation to agreements as to how we could carry out the instructions that had been written up about the work of his organs so that we could have identical updated records for military personnel and for civilians serving in the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember perhaps what came first, what the priority was, what was supposed to be done first when the personnel centres were established; do you remember that from the communication you had?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: First we worked on setting up up-to-date records. As far as I can remember, the first document that I submitted to that 30th Personnel Centre was a list of professional military personnel, as we called them then, and civilians serving in the Army of Republika Srpska including all the basic elements according to which they had been receiving their salaries until then. The next document was actually the fact that we submitted all our appointment orders for active-duty officers in the Army of Republika Srpska, and it is on that basis that they had received their salaries up until then from the computer centre. That was the beginning of this process of tallying our sets of records.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Gojko Mijic -- could Gojko Mijic ever give you any kind of order, or anyone else from that personnel centre for that matter?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Gojko Mijic and Jovo Milicic were the only colonels there, at my rank, that is, but they did not have any commanding role. This was a service of ours that was there for the purpose of collecting accurate information about officers of the Army of Republika Srpska. Our joint task was to keep the best possible up-to-date records for the personnel serving in the Army of Republika Srpska so we co-operated. He was a person I collaborated with; he wasn't my superior. Mijic was not my superior. It was Mico Grubor. Later on, it was Petar Skrbic as I said at the very outset. Mijic was just a person I worked with, a co-worker.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us go through a few more documents now. I would like to go through parts of your own personal file or dossier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have official translations for some of these document and for others we have unofficial documents [as interpreted] because it was only the other day when we received this from the OTP. But I think that we will able to deal with them with this witness. So from 65 ter [In English] 790D [Realtime transcript read in error "7907D"].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Say that again, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 00790D [Realtime transcript read in error "7907D"].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is an order on appointment issued by the minister of defence of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The date is the 16th of June, 1992. Stojan Malcic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you go on, can we just correct the transcript. It's 00790D. No 7 at the end. Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Malcic, I'm sure that this is a document that you are familiar with. So let me ask you what does it say? According to this document, when were you appointed to the particular duty mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: This is the first order on my appointment that I received in the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see two dates. One date is the 16th of June, but in the document there is also a reference to the 30th of May, 1992. Can you explain this to us?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: As I said at the outset, I came to the Main Staff on the 30th of May, 1992. At that time, there weren't any establishment books of the Main Staff. It was only when we set these books up, when we printed them, when we included our working maps, it was only then that I could be appointed to that post and be entered into this work map. And then we wrote up the orders. The order was written up only on the 16th of April, because by then establishment had been set up. Before that, we could not invent elements for my position. By now, everything was clear. So then, on the 16th of June, the Ministry of Defence signed this accurate order appointing me head of the office for personnel affairs in the administration for organisation and personnel. That is the exact name of the position I held at the time. However, it said there that I assumed that duty on the 30th of May because I actually did start working on these matters on that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down. Slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see here, Mr. Malcic, that it is mentioned that in the JNA, previously, you had Position Group 12 and now there is a reference to Position Group 10, is that what you told us about, that there could only be an increase of two position groups in terms of this new duty that you held according to establishment?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this document, you can see that the position group is 10. I could only move two groups, that is to say, from 12 to 10. And I immediately had achieved that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps do you see number 12 referred to in the last line in English? In English, PG 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see that, thank you. That's what we were looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00298, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have document - it's from the list that we have just uploaded. [In English] Doc ID 1D11-0498. Sorry it's not slash, it's dash. I only have a draft translation in hard copy, so could it please be provided to Their Honours and to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We have not received a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, do you have a copy for the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately I don't think I have any copies for the interpreters. I can only apologise to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hope they accept your apology.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, we are going to the ELMO now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As it says here this is a report on transfer of duties for Stojan Malcic, father's name Petar. The date is the 30th of May, 1992. And it says here: "I have assumed the duty of assistant chief of ..." I'm going to read it out, and I think that the interpreters will be able to follow me. In the middle it says: "I have received the duty of assistant chief of personnel department in the administration for organisation and personnel of the Main Staff of the Army of SR BH." Mr. Malcic, is this a document that was created as a consequence of the document that we saw previously, that is to say, your duty -- appointment order?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Down here it says --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, could we just scroll down a bit --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because I would like us to hear your comments. First of all, in the heading, it says, Report on transfer of duties or hand-over duties. It says, The Accounting Centre of SSNO. What is that?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: That was the Federal Secretariat for National Defence in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. This is an old form. We didn't have any others. We didn't have been opportunity of printing any others, so we just used all the old forms, and the essence had not been changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was that the document that was basic document that was sent for the payment of salaries before the personnel centre was established?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: On the basis of assign -- appointment order, we compiled this kind of document which was then sent on further for the payment of salaries. That is what is written here on the basis of the order upon which this report was written up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have this document admitted into evidence, or, rather, I would like to have it MFI'd before we receive an official translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D00299 marked for identification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we have seen these documents from May and June 1992. The next document we are going to see is from our list, and we have a translation thereof. It's 00793D from the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time, you had Position Group 10; is that right?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is an order issued by the assistant commander of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska of 6 July 1993 whereby you have been appointed standing officer of the head of the personnel department. It was signed by Colonel Mico Grubor?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When we looked at the Law on Army of Republika Srpska, I asked you to comment on Article 156 which relates to this document. I'm going to ask you now, Why was this document important for your salary?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: In July 1992, Milan Lukic, due to a serious illness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said 1992?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I thought you said 1993.

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise, 1993, but it should be 1992. In late 1992, Milan Lukic was permitted to be reunited with his family in Skopje due to a serious illness. He either retired or went to his unit, I don't know. The post of the chief of the personnel department was vacant. We waited for a certain period of time for an officer who had been colonel for a longer time than I did, and who had more experience than I did, to come and fill this post; however, this officer never turned up. And under the law, since this was a vacant post, my superior, Mico Grubor, decided to appoint me standing chief of the personnel department. And, consequently, he wrote this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see here that Position Group 8 is mentioned in this document. Did that in any way affect your salary?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes, because before I was Group 10. Now I had number 8. So I was moving up. It affected my salary because my salary was increased by these two steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please scroll down this document a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here we see in the left-hand corner a seal or a stamp, rather. It says accounting centre of the MO. Was this kind of document passed on directly to someone and to whom?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: This type of document along with the report on assumption of duties was sent to the accounting centre for the controller there to see exactly when this order was issued and what was the basis for issuing this order. The report on the assumption of duty was not sufficient for the controller.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have an exhibit number for this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do, I see below that rank 8 there's also in brackets, As per establishment PG 7. What is the meaning of that? Looks like jumping three ranks instead of two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we spoke about Galic case before, I was appointed to formation post 8; but as per establishment, it's PG 7. But I wasn't entitled to the right deriving from PG 7 because I could only move up two steps or two groups. That's how I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, that paragraph starting --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just to avoid any confusion, line 27 [sic], page -- the witness said PG 7, but I couldn't get any higher step than PG 8. That's what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know. You said line 27. Now, we don't have 27 lines. I don't know what we are talking about. Can you give me the page --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Page 76, line 20. He said that was establishment post with PG 7, but I couldn't get a higher step than PG 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Then on the same document after that PG 7, after the paragraph -- the paragraph starting "Currently as per peacetime establishment ..." it ends up that paragraph by saying "... since 10 May 1992." I thought you started on the 30th of May. How come it says 10th May?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in order to avoid any confusion created by myself because I can see both versions, this Serbian and the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let's look at both Serbian and the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, please take a look at the B/C/S version [In English] It's Cyrillic, Your Honour. [Interpretation] It says "PG 10 from 30th of May." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can see it says from 30th of May, 1992. It looks like our translations are not up to standard. Okay. So the correct date is 30th of May. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00300, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an official translation from the CLSS, the only problem was the date. But since we have corrected it in the transcript, I don't think we need to ask for correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was not attacking anybody. I was attacking the translation itself, not who did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document is also from the Defence 65 ter list. Marked [Overlapping speakers] ... 00789D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document is from July -- actually, the previous one was from July 1993, and this one is from September 1993. It's issued by minister of defence of Republika Srpska appointing you to a new post. Actually, that was the date on which you were appointed head of the personnel department and, at the same time, deputy assistant commander for organisation, mobilisation, and personnel. Based on this document, what had to be done -- but first of all, with this appointment to this new post, did you achieve or acquire any other rights on any other position group and consequently a better salary?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: In this order, we already have a sector which reflects the changes in the organisational chart of the Main Staff. And now, according to this new establishment, we had to reappointment all the officers to the duties corresponding to the new establishment. These new appointments were decided by the persons in charge, and I was appointed the head of the personnel department and at the same time the deputy head of this sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have seen this. My question was, Did you need any other document to be issued after this order?

utterances.speaker: STOJAN MALCIC
utterances.text: Yes, a report on the assumption of duty had to be compiled in order for it to be sent to the computer centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00301, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to start now on a new document. I think we can adjourn for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we adjourn, may the record show that we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis today in the absence of Judge David. I forgot to mention this at the beginning. We -- the matter will stand adjourned to tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon in Courtroom II, sir, not in the morning. But before we adjourn, I must warn you, sir, that now that you have taken the witness-stand, you may not discuss the case with anybody until you are excused from further testifying. Specifically, you may not discuss with your lawyers about the case. Okay? Matter adjourned to quarter past 2.00 tomorrow afternoon, Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.
